mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the 3-month FEDFUNDS change is not positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX returns is < 0.3 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies such as the HOUST index (goods orders) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from inventory-driven to demand-driven growth, which boosts earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% while INDPRO falls by > 5% over the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such demand-industrial production reversals.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and compressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during multi-month INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2.0% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates aggressive rate hikes, which elevates the cost of capital and dampens equity valuation multiples, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3 percentage points for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not negative (i.e., positive or flat) during such inflation spikes (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% without a corresponding rise in labor force participation suggests a tight labor market that drives wage growth and boosts corporate profits, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during sustained UNRATE declines below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business (RSAFS) demand indicators over two consecutive months predicts a resilient economic recovery that elevates earnings growth forecasts, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by > 5% over the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not positive despite the dual demand increase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a decline in the goods price deflator (not available in the provided proxies — thus this sketch is invalid per the rules) — therefore, instead: A sustained decline in the goods orders index (HOUST) below 600 suggests softening demand and supply imbalances that weigh on equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not negative (i.e., positive or flat) during sustained HOUST declines below 600.
